hindi: अब इसलिए हम विरेचन-कल्प की व्याख्या करेंगे।
english: Now, therefore, we shall explain the preparations of purgation (virecana-kalpa).

words.gloss: snuhī (Euphorbia neriifolia, a milky-sap spurge; standard)

hindi: विरेचन द्रव्यों में प्रधान ये हैं: मूलों में त्रिवृत् यानी निसोथ, त्वचाओं में तिल्वक, दूधों में स्नुही यानी सेहुंड और फलों में हरीतकी यानी हरड़।
english: Among purgation substances the foremost are: among roots, trivṛt (turpeth); among barks, tilvaka; among milks, snuhī (a spurge); among fruits, harītakī (chebulic myrobalan).

text_flags.why: possible: la for ta (harītakī is the usual drug name)

notes: kṣīra rendered literally as 'milk' (it could also mean a milky sap); the text only says 'among milks'. Distribution: each locative names the class and the nominative names the foremost item. Identification confidence: trivṛt = Operculina turpethum (standard); snuhī = Euphorbia neriifolia (standard); harītakī = Terminalia chebula (standard); tilvaka is disputed (commonly equated with lodhra, Symplocos racemosa; other identifications are proposed), so no Hindi common name is given for it.
lines_deva: विरेचनद्रव्याणां मूलेषु त्रिवृत्त्वक्षु तिल्वकः क्षीरेषु स्नुही फलेषु हरीलकी प्रधानानि
lines_iast: virecanadravyāṇāṃ mūleṣu trivṛttvakṣu tilvakaḥ kṣīreṣu snuhī phaleṣu harīlakī pradhānāni

words.gloss: of trivṛtā (= trivṛt, turpeth; see unit 2)

hindi: त्रिवृत् यानी निसोथ का मूल निश्चय ही दो प्रकार का है: लालिमायुक्त और श्याम।
english: Indeed, the root of trivṛt (turpeth) is of two kinds: reddish and dark.
notes: aruṇa 'reddish' and śyāma 'dark' are colour words; the text names them as the two kinds.
lines_deva: त्रिवृतायाः खलु द्विविधं मूलमरुणं श्यामं च
lines_iast: trivṛtāyāḥ khalu dvividhaṃ mūlamaruṇaṃ śyāmaṃ ca

words.gloss: in the young, aged, delicate and soft-koṣṭha

hindi: उन दोनों में लालिमायुक्त मूल कषाय और मधुर है, विपाक में कटु है, रूक्ष है और कफ तथा पित्त को हरने वाला है; फिर विशेष विधि से तैयार करने पर सब व्याधियों को शान्त करने वाला है; सुखपूर्वक विरेचन कराने के कारण शिशु, वृद्ध, सुकुमार और मृदु कोष्ठ वालों में प्रशस्त है; और वह 'त्रिवृत्' शब्द से कहा जाता है।
english: Of these two, the reddish one is astringent and sweet, pungent in vipāka (the post-digestive stage), dry, and removes Kapha (śleṣman) and Pitta; moreover, through a particular preparation it pacifies all ailments; because it purges easily, it is recommended in the young, the aged, the delicate and those whose koṣṭha (abdomen, bowel) is soft; and it is what is denoted by the word trivṛt.
notes: kaṣāya here is the taste 'astringent' (not 'decoction'; cf. GLOSSARY OPEN item kaṣāya/kvātha/niryūha). śleṣman = Kapha (synonym). The long compound śiśu-sthavira-sukumāra-mṛdu-koṣṭheṣu may be read as persons (the young, the aged, the delicate) plus 'those of soft koṣṭha', or all four as qualifying koṣṭha; rendered as persons. 'kalpanā-viśeṣāt' = from a particular manner of preparation, not specified here. vipāka, koṣṭha kept with a gloss.
lines_deva: तत्रारुणं कषायमधुरं विपाके कटुकं रूक्षं श्लेष्मपित्तहरं कल्पनाविशेषात्पुनः सर्वव्याधिशमनं सुखविरेचनत्वाच्छिशुस्थविरसुकुमारमृदुकोष्ठेषु प्रशस्तं त्रिवृच्छब्दवाच्यं च
lines_iast: tatrāruṇaṃ kaṣāyamadhuraṃ vipāke kaṭukaṃ rūkṣaṃ śleṣmapittaharaṃ kalpanāviśeṣātpunaḥ sarvavyādhiśamanaṃ sukhavirecanatvācchiśusthavirasukumāramṛdukoṣṭheṣu praśastaṃ trivṛcchabdavācyaṃ ca

words.gloss: in those with many doṣas, able to bear distress, with hard koṣṭha

hindi: दूसरा मूल भी उससे गुणों में कुछ हीन है, तीक्ष्ण है, कण्ठ और हृदय को खींचने वाला है, मूर्च्छा और सम्मोह करने वाला है; दोषों को शीघ्र हरने के कारण बहुत दोष वाले, क्लेश सहने में समर्थ और कठोर कोष्ठ वालों में प्रशस्त है; और वह 'श्यामा' शब्द से कहा जाता है।
english: The other one too is somewhat inferior to that in qualities; it is sharp, pulls at the throat and heart, and causes fainting and bewilderment; because it quickly removes the doṣas, it is recommended in those with many doṣas, who can bear distress, and whose koṣṭha (abdomen, bowel) is hard; and it is what is denoted by the word śyāmā.

text_flags.why: possible: va for ba in 'bahu' (the edition confuses ba and va)

notes: āśu 'quickly' may go with mūrcchā-saṃmoha-kṛt or with doṣa-haratvāt; rendered with the latter. krūra-koṣṭha rendered 'hard koṣṭha' (krūra lit. 'cruel, harsh'). The compound bahu-doṣa-kleśa-kṣama-krūra-koṣṭheṣu is read as three descriptions of persons (many doṣas; bearing distress; harsh koṣṭha).
lines_deva: इतरदपि तस्माद्गुणैः किंचिद्धीनं तीक्ष्णं कंठहृदयकर्षणं मूर्च्छासंमोहकृदाशु दोषहरत्वाद्वहुदोषक्लेशक्षमक्रूरकोष्ठेषु प्रशस्तं श्यामाशब्दवाच्यं च
lines_iast: itaradapi tasmādguṇaiḥ kiṃciddhīnaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ kaṃṭhahṛdayakarṣaṇaṃ mūrcchāsaṃmohakṛdāśu doṣaharatvādvahudoṣakleśakṣamakrūrakoṣṭheṣu praśastaṃ śyāmāśabdavācyaṃ ca

hindi: अब उन दोनों में से जो मूल तिरछा फैला हुआ न हो, गहराई में गया हुआ और चिकना हो, उसे संग्रह करे।
english: Now, of the two, one should collect the root that is not spread out sideways, has gone deep, and is smooth.
notes: āharet rendered 'collect' (lit. 'bring, fetch').

hindi: फिर छाल को सुखाकर भली-भाँति रख ले।
english: Then, having dried the bark, one should keep it properly.

words.gloss: combined with śuṇṭhī (dried ginger, Zingiber officinale; standard) and saindhava (rock salt)

hindi: उस चूर्ण को शुण्ठी यानी सोंठ और सैन्धव यानी सेंधा नमक से युक्त करके, अम्ल पदार्थों के साथ अथवा मांस-रस के साथ भी, वात के रोगों में पीना चाहिए।
english: In ailments of Vāta one should drink that powder, combined with śuṇṭhī (dried ginger) and saindhava (rock salt), with sour things or also with meat juice.
notes: amlaiḥ is left as 'sour things' (the text names no particular sour substances). Alternative: 'with sour (liquids)'.

words.gloss: milk, honey, drākṣā (grape or raisin, Vitis vinifera; standard), ikṣu (sugarcane, Saccharum officinarum; standard), juice of kāśmarya (Gmelina arborea; standard), ghee

hindi: पित्त से उत्पन्न रोगों में, दूध, मधु, द्राक्षा यानी अंगूर, इक्षु यानी गन्ना, काश्मर्य यानी गम्भारी का स्वरस और घृत मिलाकर, मधुर क्वाथों के साथ तथा शर्करा सहित, उसे पिए।
english: In (ailments) arising from Pitta, (one should drink it) with milk, honey, drākṣā (grape), ikṣu (sugarcane), the expressed juice of kāśmarya (gmelina), and ghee, with sweet decoctions, and with sugar.

text_flags.why: possible: kāthaiḥ for kvāthaiḥ (decoctions); 'kātha' is not a known word

notes: The verb 'pibet' is carried over from unit 8 (the sentence continues); the compound kṣīra-...-sarpiḥ is read as a dvandva list of things mixed in. 'pitta-uttheṣu' lit. 'risen from Pitta', noun (roges) supplied. kvātha = decoction (GLOSSARY). GROUPING: unit 9 continues the sentence of unit 8; units 8, 9 and 10 each give a different Vāta/Pitta/Kapha use of the same powder. As printed, 'sarpiḥ' (n. nom./acc. sg.) cannot itself be instrumental, yet the list is translated with 'with'. Either an instrumental (sarpirbhiḥ) is intended, or the list is one long instrumental compound running on through 'svādu-kvāthaiḥ' (… -svarasa-sarpiḥ-svādu-kvāthaiḥ), the printed space being a spacing slip. Sense unchanged.

words.gloss: with urine, honey, kṣāra (alkali), ariṣṭa (fermented medicinal liquor), juice of pīlu (Salvadora persica; probable), and decoctions of triphalā (the three myrobalans) and of pañcakola (the five-kola group)
mixed through with powder of vyoṣa (the three pungents)

hindi: कफ से उत्पन्न रोगों में, मूत्र, मधु, क्षार यानी खार, अरिष्ट यानी किण्वित औषधीय पेय, पीलु का रस, तथा त्रिफला यानी हरड़, बहेड़ा और आँवला और पंचकोल यानी पीपर, पिपलामूल, चव्य, चित्रक और सोंठ के क्वाथों के साथ, व्योष यानी सोंठ, पीपर और काली मिर्च के चूर्ण में मिलाकर, उसे पिए।
english: In (ailments) born of Kapha, (one should drink it) with urine, honey, alkali (kṣāra), ariṣṭa (fermented medicinal liquor), pīlu juice, and the decoctions of triphalā (the three myrobalans) and of pañcakola (the five-kola group), mixed through with vyoṣa (the three pungents) powder.

text_flags.why: possible: yoṣa for vyoṣa (v dropped; 'yoṣa' = woman makes no sense here, and unit 11 has vyoṣa)

notes: 'pibet' carried over from unit 8. Technical names kept: kṣāra (alkali), ariṣṭa, pīlu, triphalā (three fruits), pañcakola (five kola), vyoṣa (drug-group name). Which urine is not stated. The dvandva of 'kvāthaiḥ' may be read so that only the last two are decoctions; rendered as above. GROUPING: continues the sentence of units 8-9. The printed 'kkathair' may stand for kāthair (the spelling seen in unit 9, svādukāthaiḥ) or kvāthair; in either case the sense is 'decoctions'. Group members and identifications (each given once for this chunk): triphalā = harītakī, bibhītaka (Terminalia bellirica) and āmalaka (Phyllanthus emblica) (standard). vyoṣa = śuṇṭhī, pippalī (Piper longum) and marica (Piper nigrum) (standard). pañcakola = pippalī, pippalīmūla (root of pippalī), cavya (Piper retrofractum, probable), citraka (Plumbago zeylanica, standard) and śuṇṭhī (standard). pīlu = Salvadora persica (probable; other trees have been proposed). ariṣṭa = a fermented medicinal liquor (standard class). kṣāra = an alkaline preparation, usually from plant ash (standard); which kṣāra is not stated.

words.gloss: sweet with ghee, sugar, akṣoḍa (walnut, Juglans regia; standard), tavakṣīrī (disputed: Curcuma angustifolia starch, or bamboo manna)

sour with the juice of mātuluṅga (citron, Citrus medica; standard), dāḍima (pomegranate, Punica granatum; standard), āmalaka (emblic myrobalan, see unit 10), kola (jujube, Ziziphus jujuba; probable), karamardaka (karaunda, Carissa carandas; standard), kapittha (wood-apple, Limonia acidissima; standard), and buttermilk (takra)
filled with various vesavāra (a spiced preparation, traditionally of boned minced meat; probable)

fragrant with sahakāra (mango, Mangifera indica; standard) juice, trijātaka (cinnamon bark, Cinnamomum verum; cardamom, Elettaria cardamomum; bay leaf, Cinnamomum tamala; standard), nāgakeśara (Mesua ferrea stamens; standard), karpūra (camphor, Cinnamomum camphora; standard)

hindi: और इन्हीं द्रव्यों से, अपने-अपने अनुसार, लेह, गुटिका, मोदक, भक्ष्य और भोज्य पदार्थ तैयार करे: जो घृत, शर्करा, अक्षोड यानी अखरोट और तवक्षीरी से मधुर हों; मातुलुंग यानी बिजौरा नींबू, दाडिम यानी अनार, आमलक यानी आँवला, कोल यानी बेर, करमर्दक यानी करौंदा और कपित्थ यानी कैथ के रस तथा तक्र यानी छाछ से अम्ल हों; सैन्धव यानी सेंधा नमक से लवणयुक्त हों; व्योष यानी सोंठ, पीपर और काली मिर्च से तीक्ष्ण हों; नाना प्रकार के वेसवार से भरे हों; और सहकार यानी आम के रस, त्रिजातक यानी दालचीनी, इलायची और तेजपात, नागकेशर तथा कर्पूर यानी कपूर से सुगन्धित हों; इस प्रकार।
english: And with these very substances, each according to its own, one should prepare lehas (licked preparations), pills, modakas, and bhakṣya and bhojya foods: sweet with ghee, sugar, akṣoḍa (walnut) and tavakṣīrī; sour with the juice of mātuluṅga (citron), dāḍima (pomegranate), āmalaka (emblic myrobalan), kola (jujube), karamardaka (karaunda) and kapittha (wood-apple), and with buttermilk; salty with saindhava (rock salt); sharp with vyoṣa (the three pungents); filled with various vesavāra (a spiced preparation); and fragrant with sahakāra (mango) juice, trijātaka (cinnamon bark, cardamom and bay leaf), nāgakeśara (Ceylon ironwood stamens) and karpūra (camphor); thus.

text_flags.why: possible: vowels and ka dropped in the scan (kola, karamardaka, kapittha)
extra anusvāra after bhojyā (ā + ṃ + ny); read bhojyāni upakalpayet

notes: yathāsvam 'each according to its own' (its own property is not specified). kinds of taste named by the compounds: sweet, sour, salty, sharp (tīkṣṇa lit. 'sharp'); the text names no bitter or astringent group. vesavāra: preparation name kept. All drug names kept in the translation; identifications are given beside them in the word glosses with confidence words (tavakṣīrī disputed; kola, vesavāra probable; the rest standard). 'iti' closes the instruction and is rendered 'thus'. The word split of the first compound is uncertain: ghṛta-śarkarā-akṣoḍa-tavakṣīrī-madhurāṇi could also be read as 'ghee, sugar, akṣoḍa, tavakṣīrī, and sweet things'; the parallel with the next compounds (X-amlāni, X-lavaṇāni, X-tīkṣṇāni) favours 'sweet with'. Foods bhakṣya (to be chewed) and bhojya (to be eaten) kept as the two classes.
lines_deva: एभिरेव च द्रव्यैर्यथास्वं घृतशर्कराक्षोडतवक्षीरीमधुराणि मातुलुंगदाडिमामलककोल्करमर्द्ककपित्थरसतक्राम्लानि सैंधवलवणानि व्योषतीक्ष्णानि विविधवेसवारपूरितानि सहकाररसत्रिजातकनागकेशरकपूरसुरभीणि लेहगुटिकामोदकभक्ष्यभोज्यांन्युपकल्पयेदिति
lines_iast: ebhireva ca dravyairyathāsvaṃ ghṛtaśarkarākṣoḍatavakṣīrīmadhurāṇi mātuluṃgadāḍimāmalakakolkaramardkakapittharasatakrāmlāni saiṃdhavalavaṇāni vyoṣatīkṣṇāni vividhavesavārapūritāni sahakārarasatrijātakanāgakeśarakapūrasurabhīṇi lehaguṭikāmodakabhakṣyabhojyāṃnyupakalpayediti

hindi: और इस विषय में यह है।
english: And in this matter there is this (verse).
notes: Introductory formula 'bhavati cātra' ('and here there is ...'); it introduces the verses of units 13-37. GROUPING: this is a formula unit that introduces the following verse(s); it belongs with unit 13.

words.gloss: with a decoction of trivṛt paste

hindi: त्रिवृत् के कल्क के क्वाथ से सिद्ध किया हुआ, शर्करा सहित हिम,
english: A hima (cold preparation), prepared with a decoction of trivṛt paste (kalka), together with sugar,
notes: kaṣāya here = decoction (GLOSSARY: all 'decoction'; OPEN whether to keep kaṣāya/kvātha/niryūha apart). kalka = paste. trivṛt-kalka-kaṣāya may mean 'decoction made with trivṛt paste' or 'paste and decoction of trivṛt'; rendered as the first. sita 'white' taken as sugar. hima lit. 'cold'; kept with a gloss. GROUPING: units 13 and 14 form one verse and one sentence (hima ... is a lick, a heart-pleasing purgative).

words.gloss: combined with honey and trijāta (read as trijātaka: cinnamon bark, cardamom, bay leaf; probable)

hindi: मधु और त्रिजात यानी दालचीनी, इलायची और तेजपात से मिला हुआ लेह हृदय को प्रिय विरेचन है।
english: Combined with honey and trijāta (the three aromatics: cinnamon bark, cardamom, bay leaf), the leha (licked preparation) is a heart-pleasing purgative.

text_flags.why: ṭrī for tri (misprint); trijāta (as trijātaka in unit 11) is the drug-group name

notes: hṛdyam lit. 'of/for the heart, agreeable'; kept as 'heart-pleasing'. trijāta = drug-group name, kept. GROUPING: unit 14 completes the verse begun in unit 13.

words.gloss: ajagandhā (disputed: Gynandropsis gynandra or other plants), tavakṣīrī (disputed, see unit 11), vidārī (Pueraria tuberosa, Indian kudzu tuber; probable), sugar, trivṛt

hindi: अजगन्धा, तवक्षीरी, विदारी यानी विदारीकन्द, शर्करा और त्रिवृत्,
english: Ajagandhā, tavakṣīrī, vidārī (kudzu tuber), sugar (śarkarā) and trivṛt,
notes: Drug names kept. The list continues into unit 16. GROUPING: units 15 and 16 form one verse and one sentence (these, powdered and licked with honey and ghee, one is well purged).

hindi: चूर्ण बनाकर मधु और घृत के साथ चाट लेने पर मनुष्य भली-भाँति विरेचित होता है।
english: Powdered and licked up with honey and ghee, one is well purged.

text_flags.why: dhyā for bhyā (misprint); instrumental dual of madhu-sarpis

notes: viricyate is impersonal passive; 'one' (a person) supplied.

words.gloss: afflicted by sannipāta (all three doṣas deranged together), fever (jvara), stiffness (stambha), thirst (pipāsā) and burning (dāha)

hindi: सन्निपात यानी तीनों दोषों का एक साथ कुपित होना, ज्वर यानी बुखार, स्तम्भ यानी जकड़न, पिपासा यानी प्यास और दाह यानी जलन से पीड़ित,
english: One afflicted by sannipāta (derangement of all three doṣas together), fever (jvara), stiffness (stambha), thirst and burning (dāha),
notes: sannipāta-jvara may be one term ('sannipāta-fever') or two ('sannipāta' and 'fever'); rendered as two members, alternative noted. stambha lit. 'stiffness'. GROUPING: units 17 and 18 form one verse; unit 19 continues the same sentence.

words.gloss: a joint-piece of ikṣu made two-fold

hindi: दो भागों में किए हुए इक्षु-खण्ड के भीतर त्रिवृत् का लेप करे,
english: should smear, inside, with trivṛt, a piece (joint) of ikṣu that has been split in two,
notes: gaṇḍikā 'piece, joint-section' rendered 'piece'. Object (ikṣu-piece) and 'inside' together: the inside of the split piece is smeared with trivṛt. Gender: the printed ending -ṃ is read as n. acc. sg. (ikṣugaṇḍikā would be f.). ikṣu kept as a name.

hindi: और उसे एक करके, पुटपाक से स्विन्न किया हुआ, खाए।
english: and having joined it into one, one should eat that, steamed by puṭa-cooking.
notes: puṭapāka = cooking in a wrapped parcel (puṭa 'fold, wrapping'); kept literal as 'puṭa-cooking'. GROUPING: unit 19 is a single line completing the sentence of units 17-18; no partner line for a second half-verse is evident (unit 20 begins a new recipe), so the print may have a verse of three lines here or a line is missing.

words.gloss: with bhṛṅga (bhṛṅgarāja, Eclipta prostrata; probable) and elā (small cardamom, Elettaria cardamomum; standard)

hindi: भृंग यानी भांगरा और एला यानी इलायची के बराबर नीली यानी नील, उनके साथ त्रिवृत् और उनके साथ शर्करा।
english: Nīlī (indigo) equal to bhṛṅga and elā (cardamom); with those, trivṛt; and with those, sugar.
notes: The measure relations are not stated clearly: 'taiḥ' (instrumental 'with/by those') occurs twice; probably 'trivṛt equal to those and sugar equal to those', but kept literal. Drug names kept. GROUPING: units 20 and 21 appear to form one verse (unit 21 gives the powder and its drink).

words.gloss: with fruit juice, honey and saktu (flour of roasted grain, commonly barley)

hindi: चूर्ण को फल के रस, मधु और सक्तु यानी सत्तू के साथ तर्पण रूप में पिए।
english: One should drink the powder as a tarpaṇa (satiating draught), with fruit juice, honey and saktu (flour of roasted grain, commonly barley).
notes: tarpaṇa lit. 'satisfying'; kept with a gloss. saktu kept with a gloss; no identification of the grain. 'phala-rasa' = juice of fruit(s), kind unspecified.

words.gloss: in those arising from Vāta, Pitta and Kapha

hindi: वात, पित्त और कफ से उत्पन्न रोगों में, तथा अल्प अग्नि वालों में,
english: In ailments arising from Vāta, Pitta and Kapha, and in those with little fire (anala),
notes: anala lit. 'fire' (the digestive fire is probably meant; not stated in the text). alpānaleṣu is read as persons ('those with little fire'). GROUPING: units 22 and 23 form one verse.

hindi: और सुकुमार मनुष्यों में यह निरपाय विरेचन है।
english: and in delicate men, it is a harmless purgation.
notes: 'nirapāya' lit. 'without loss/danger'; rendered 'harmless'. The subject (the preparation of units 20-21) is understood.

words.gloss: viḍaṅga (false black pepper, Embelia ribes; standard) grains, varā, yāvaśūka, kaṇā (= pippalī, long pepper; standard)

hindi: विडंग यानी वायविडंग के दाने, वरा, यावशूक, कणा यानी पीपर और त्रिवृत्,
english: Viḍaṅga (false black pepper) grains, varā, yāvaśūka, kaṇā (long pepper) and trivṛt,
notes: Drug names kept. taṇḍula lit. 'grain'; could instead be a separate member ('viḍaṅga, taṇḍula'). varā lit. 'excellent' (used as a name); kaṇā lit. 'grain, particle' (used as a name). GROUPING: units 24 and 25 form one verse. varā is disputed (often read as triphalā, but its sense is also 'excellent'); yāvaśūka is probably yavakṣāra (barley-ash alkali) per commentators (probable). Neither is translated further because this unit has low confidence.

hindi: सब का आधा भाग लेकर, वह चूर्ण मधु और घृत के साथ अथवा गुड़ के साथ।
english: (Taking) half of the whole, that powder with honey and ghee, or with jaggery.

text_flags.why: possible: 'cīṭha' is not a Sanskrit word; cū-r-ṇa misread as cī-ṭha ('that powder')

notes: 'sarvataḥ ardhena' is obscure: 'with half on all sides / half of the whole'; the point is probably that trivṛt is half of the total of the other drugs of unit 24, but the text does not say so. Verb understood (take/drink). GROUPING: continues unit 24.

words.gloss: plīhodara (spleen enlargement with swollen belly; standard)
halīmaka (a severe stage of pāṇḍu, pale-yellow jaundiced condition; probable)
arocaka (lack of relish, loss of appetite; standard)

hindi: गुल्म यानी पेट की गाँठ, प्लीहोदर यानी तिल्ली बढ़ने के साथ पेट फूलना, कास यानी खाँसी, हलीमक यानी पाण्डु रोग की उग्र अवस्था, अरोचक यानी भोजन में अरुचि,
english: gulma (abdominal lump), plīhodara (spleen enlargement with swollen belly), cough (kāsa), halīmaka (a severe stage of the pale-yellow pāṇḍu condition), arocaka (lack of relish, loss of appetite),

text_flags.why: m moved to the next word (word-division error); the pair is halīmakam arocakam

notes: Ailment names kept as Sanskrit terms with modern equivalents beside them (gulma: abdominal lump, standard; plīhodara: spleen enlargement with swollen belly, standard; halīmaka: a severe stage of pāṇḍu, probable; arocaka: loss of appetite, standard). 'kāsa' glossed 'cough', arocaka lit. 'lack of relish'. GROUPING: units 26 and 27 form one verse; the subject (the preparation of units 24-25) is the one that 'wipes away' these in unit 27.

words.gloss: the rutas of Kapha and Vāta (reading doubtful)

hindi: और कफ तथा वात के रुत एवं अन्य बहुत से गदों को वह पोंछ डालता है।
english: and it wipes away the rutas of Kapha and Vāta, and many other ailments (gada).

text_flags.why: possible: ruta (cry, sound) is odd; ruj (pain) may be intended; not certain

notes: 'ruta' is kept as printed; its literal sense is 'cry, sound', so the phrase is doubtful (perhaps 'pains'). The grammar of kapha-vāta-rutān ca anyān gadān bahūn may also be 'the Kapha-Vāta ailments and many other ailments'. parimārṣṭi lit. 'wipes off'.

words.gloss: viḍaṅga (see unit 24), root of pippalī (long pepper), triphalā (the three myrobalans, see unit 10), dhānya (coriander seed, dhānyaka; probable), citraka (leadwort, see unit 10)

hindi: विडंग यानी वायविडंग, पिप्पली यानी पीपर का मूल, त्रिफला यानी हरड़, बहेड़ा और आँवला, धान्य यानी धनिया और चित्रक यानी चीता,
english: Viḍaṅga, the root of pippalī (long pepper), triphalā (the three myrobalans), dhānya (coriander) and citraka (leadwort),
notes: Drug names kept; 'pippalī-mūla' may be taken as one drug name ('pippalīmūla') or 'root of pippalī'; rendered as the second. dhānya lit. 'grain'; kept as a name. GROUPING: units 28 and 29 form one verse (a list of drugs); the sentence continues in units 30-33. dhānya = coriander (dhānyaka, Coriandrum sativum) is the usual reading in drug lists (probable); the plain sense 'grain' remains possible.

words.gloss: marica (black pepper), indrayava (seeds of kuṭaja, Holarrhena antidysenterica; standard), ajājī (cumin, Cuminum cyminum; standard), pippalī (long pepper), hastipippalī (elephant pepper, Scindapsus officinalis; probable)

hindi: मरिच यानी काली मिर्च, इन्द्रयव यानी इन्द्रजौ, अजाजी यानी जीरा, पिप्पली यानी पीपर और हस्तिपिप्पली यानी गजपीपल,
english: Marica (black pepper), indrayava (kuṭaja seeds), ajājī (cumin), pippalī (long pepper) and hastipippalī (elephant pepper),
notes: Drug names kept (indrayava lit. 'Indra's barley', hastipippalī lit. 'elephant pippalī', used as names). The list continues into unit 30.

words.gloss: dīpyaka (disputed: ajwain, Trachyspermum ammi, or ajamodā)

hindi: दीप्यक और पाँच लवण, चूर्ण किए हुए, प्रत्येक एक कर्ष, अलग-अलग,
english: Dīpyaka and the five salts, powdered, one karṣa (a measure) each, separately,
notes: karṣa = a measure of weight, kept. The five salts are not named here. GROUPING: units 30 and 31 form one verse. paṃcalavaṇa (the five salts) is conventionally sauvarcala, saindhava, sāmudra, viḍa and audbhida, but the lists differ between texts (probable); the verse does not name them.

words.gloss: the portions of tila (sesame) oil and of trivṛt powder

hindi: और तिल के तेल और त्रिवृत् के चूर्ण के दो भाग, आठ-आठ पल नापे हुए,
english: and the two portions, of tila (sesame) oil and of trivṛt powder, each measured as eight palas,
notes: pala = a measure of weight, kept. tila = sesame (Sesamum indicum; standard). Dual 'bhāgau' = the two portions.

words.gloss: prasthas of the juice of dhātrī fruit (dhātrī = āmalaka, emblic myrobalan; standard)
joined with half a tulā of jaggery

hindi: धात्री यानी आँवले के फल के रस के तीन प्रस्थ, आधा तुला गुड़ से युक्त,
english: three prasthas of the juice of dhātrī (emblic myrobalan) fruit, joined with half a tulā of jaggery,

text_flags.why: extra anusvāra after tulā, and final -āna for -ān

notes: prastha and tulā are measures, kept. dhātrī (lit. 'nurse') is a standard synonym of āmalakī/āmalaka, the emblic myrobalan. In the standard measure system a tulā is 100 palas. GROUPING: units 32 and 33 form one verse.

hindi: मृदु अग्नि पर पकाकर फिर मात्रा के अनुसार खाए, बिना नियन्त्रण के।
english: Having cooked it on a mild fire, one should then eat it in measure, unrestrained.
notes: mātrām may also go with ayantraṇaḥ ('without restriction of measure'); the plain reading is adopted. a-yantraṇa lit. 'without restraint/restriction' (no further sense given in the text).

words.gloss: difficulty of urine (mūtrakṛcchra; painful or obstructed urination, dysuria)

hindi: मन्द अग्नि होना यानी पाचन की कमजोरी, ज्वर यानी बुखार, मूर्च्छा यानी बेहोशी, मूत्रकृच्छ्र यानी पेशाब में कठिनाई, अरोचक यानी भोजन में अरुचि,
english: slowness of fire (weak digestion), fever (jvara), fainting (mūrcchā), mūtrakṛcchra (difficulty of urine, dysuria), lack of relish (arocaka, loss of appetite),

text_flags.why: possible: final anusvāra dropped (accusative like the other items)
possible: arocake (loc.) for arocakaṃ (acc.), the list is accusative; or 'arocake' read as 'in arocaka'

notes: The verb 'hanti' is in unit 36 (the object list runs through units 34-36). mandāgnitva lit. 'state of slow fire'. If 'arocake' is kept as printed (locative) it would mean 'in arocaka'. GROUPING: units 34 and 35 form one verse; the list of objects runs on to unit 36.

words.gloss: kuṣṭha (skin diseases, including leprosy), arśas (haemorrhoids, piles), kāmalā (jaundice), meha (urinary disorders of the prameha class, which includes diabetes), gulma (abdominal lump), udara (belly; here the belly-disease class), bhagandara (anal fistula)

hindi: कुष्ठ यानी त्वचा के रोग जिनमें कोढ़ भी है, अर्श यानी बवासीर, कामला यानी पीलिया, मेह यानी प्रमेह जिसमें मधुमेह भी आता है, गुल्म यानी पेट की गाँठ, उदर यानी पेट का रोग और भगंदर यानी गुदा के पास का नासूर,
english: kuṣṭha (skin diseases, including leprosy), arśas (haemorrhoids), kāmalā (jaundice), meha (urinary disorders of the prameha class, including diabetes), gulma (abdominal lump), udara (belly, as a disease class) and bhagandara (anal fistula),
notes: Ailment names kept in Sanskrit with modern equivalents beside them, all standard: kuṣṭha is a class of skin diseases that includes leprosy; meha/prameha is the urinary class that includes diabetes mellitus; udara in a list of ailments is the belly disease class (abdominal enlargement); bhagandara is fistula-in-ano. The visarga in 'arśaḥkāmalā' is regular sandhi (arśas + kāmalā; visarga stays before k); the stem is arśas. udara 'belly'; meha lit. 'urinating'.

words.gram: dvandva; first part of grahaṇī-pāṇḍu-rogān (m. acc. pl.)

hindi: ग्रहणी और पाण्डु रोगों को नष्ट करता है, और वह पुंसवन भी है।
english: It destroys the grahaṇī and pāṇḍu (pale) ailments, and it is a puṃsavana (male-begetting).

text_flags.why: possible: pāṇḍu-rogān misread as pāṃ + du-rogān (ṇḍu broken across two words)

notes: Hindi rendering of 'pāṇḍu' kept as the Sanskrit term. The reading grahaṇī-pāṇḍu-rogān is conjectural; as printed the words make no sense ('durogān' lit. 'bad ailments' could be read, 'grahaṇīpāṃ' not). puṃsavana lit. 'bringing forth a male', kept. GROUPING: units 36 and 37 form one verse; 'saḥ' refers to the guḍa Kalyāṇaka named in unit 37. For the surest words only: grahaṇī is a disorder of digestion with disturbed stools (chronic diarrhoea or malabsorption type) and pāṇḍu is the pale condition (anaemia or jaundice type), both standard equivalents; the rest of the reading stays conjectural and is not enriched.

hindi: कल्याणक नामक गुड़ सभी ऋतुओं में प्रयोग के योग्य है।
english: The guḍa named Kalyāṇaka is applicable in all seasons.
notes: Kalyāṇaka is a name (lit. 'auspicious'). yaugika lit. 'fit for use, applicable'. The recipe is units 28-33; its uses units 34-36.
